ai.title: AI Chat and Agent UI Components for React
ai.description: Interface pieces for chat and agent products. The set covers the whole conversation: a composer with a model picker, a message that streams in, a collapsible reasoning trace, cards for tool calls and approvals, a plan that fills as steps complete, and an assembled chat that ties them together.

faq.question: Do the AI components work with the Vercel AI SDK or my own streaming endpoint?
faq.answer: Either. They take plain props (messages, a streaming string, tool-call state) and do not import any AI SDK, so you wire them to the Vercel AI SDK, LangChain, or a hand-rolled fetch stream.

faq.question: How do I install the components in AI?
faq.answer: With the shadcn CLI. Each component page lists its exact command: free components install from a public URL (npx shadcn add https://useplanes.com/r/<name>.json), Pro components install by name (npx shadcn add @useplanes/<name>) after npx @useplanes/cli init --key <key>.

faq.question: Do they work with Next.js App Router and Tailwind CSS v4?
faq.answer: Yes. Every component is a React 19 client component styled with Tailwind CSS v4, and works in Next.js App Router, Vite, or any React app with Tailwind CSS v4.

faq.question: Are the components in AI free?
faq.answer: 1 of the 12 are free. The rest need a one-time Planes Pro license, which covers every component and future additions.

faq.question: What do they depend on?
faq.answer: Motion (formerly Framer Motion) is the only runtime animation dependency. The CLI writes the .tsx source into your project, so there is no Planes package to keep updated.

webgl.title: WebGL Shader Backgrounds for React
webgl.description: Full-viewport backdrops, each a single React component with no Three.js dependency, all but one rendered in a fragment shader (Beams is pure CSS). Light effects like a logo flare and a prism, fluid and smoke simulations, embers and streaks, a cloud deck seen from altitude, and a ray-marched torus quantized into terminal glyphs.

faq.question: Will the WebGL backgrounds slow the page down?
faq.answer: The shader backdrops render on the GPU in a single full-screen quad, pause when off screen or hidden, cap pixel density on all but Ink, and fall back to a plain background when WebGL is unavailable or reduced motion is set. Beams is pure CSS with no canvas at all.

controls.title: Animated React Controls: Pickers, Inputs, and Menus
controls.description: Inputs and menus that respond physically. A date picker and a searchable select, a number stepper with rolling digits, a one-time-code input, segmented tabs with a stretching pill, a nested command palette, an iOS-style bottom sheet with detents, a rotary knob, and a few playful pieces like a receipt printer and an elastic drag-select.

faq.question: Are the controls accessible form inputs?
faq.answer: The form controls are. The date picker, select, number stepper, OTP input, segmented control, command palette and knob are keyboard-operable with matching ARIA roles (grid, combobox, spinbutton, tablist, slider), built on native inputs where one exists, with the animation layered on top. Playful pieces like the receipt printer and scratch card are visual, not inputs.

carousels.title: Animated React Carousel Components
carousels.description: Ways to move a row of content past the viewer. A 3D cover flow you can drag or scroll, a cylinder and an arc that curve the row, a wheel that blurs everything but the frame in focus, a gallery that stretches the hovered frame, a parallax marquee, a velocity-driven marquee, and a logo wall that cycles cell by cell.

faq.question: Do the carousels support touch, keyboard and reduced motion?
faq.answer: Drag and swipe on touch, arrow keys on the carousels that have a focused frame (Cover Flow, Image Wheel, Focus Scale, Elastic), and every one respects prefers-reduced-motion by removing the non-essential motion.

physics.title: Physics-Based React Animation Components
physics.description: Motion that comes from simulation rather than keyframes. Pendulums that drift in and out of phase, wavefronts spreading across a grid, particles converging into text, a Rubik's cube you can twist, and dot fields that scatter from the cursor and snap back.

faq.question: How are the physics simulated?
faq.answer: With Motion springs and small hand-written simulations in requestAnimationFrame. There is no physics engine dependency, and every piece respects prefers-reduced-motion.

text.title: Animated Text Effects for React
text.description: Eight ways to animate type. A split-flap board that flips through characters mechanically, a stagger that resolves new text glyph by glyph on hover, a film-title reveal where each word settles out of a blur, a headline filled with flowing liquid, a signature drawn stroke by stroke, a rainbow band that sweeps across a line, neon tubing that strikes on letter by letter, and an odometer where only the digits that change roll.

faq.question: Do the text effects hurt SEO or screen readers?
faq.answer: No. The real text stays in the DOM as plain characters or with an accessible label, so search engines and screen readers read the words while the animation runs on top.
